edges.description: Sialylated lipooligosaccharide on the C. jejuni envelope resembles the ganglioside epitopes of peripheral nerve closely enough that one antibody response recognises both. The cited sentence names that mimicry outright rather than leaving it to be inferred, which is why this link is direct where the other two antecedent infections in this entry are not.

A frequent antecedent infection, but the route by which it reaches an antiganglioside response is not established the way the Campylobacter route is. Graded identically to the Zika link in this entry, since both rest on an antecedent association with no mechanism named.

Outbreak-associated incidence rises are strong evidence that Zika precedes the syndrome and weak evidence about how. Graded identically to the cytomegalovirus link in this entry, which rests on the same kind of antecedent association.

evidence.reference_title: Role of Campylobacter jejuni infection in the pathogenesis of Guillain-Barré syndrome: an update.
evidence.snippet: Thus, C. jejuni is now considered as a major triggering agent of GBS. Molecular mimicry between sialylated lipooligosaccharide structures on the cell envelope of these bacteria and ganglioside epitopes on the human nerves that generates cross-reactive immune response results in autoimmune-driven nerve damage.

nodes.description: Antibody binding activates complement cascade, leading to membrane attack complex deposition on Schwann cells and nodes of Ranvier. This causes demyelination in AIDP or axonal damage in AMAN/AMSAN variants.

evidence.reference_title: Anti-ganglioside antibodies can bind peripheral nerve nodes of Ranvier and activate the complement cascade without inducing acute conduction block in vitro.
evidence.snippet: These data indicate that anti-ganglioside antibodies can diffuse into a desheathed nerve, bind to nodes of Ranvier and fix complement in vitro without resulting in any overt physiological deterioration of the nerve over 4-6 h.

evidence.reference_title: Immune attack on the Schwann cell surface in acute inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy.
evidence.snippet: Many fibers had a rim of the complement activation marker C3d and the terminal complement complex neoantigen C5b-9 along the outer surface of the Schwann cells.

evidence.snippet: The most frequent pathogens involved are C. jejuni, cytomegalovirus (CMV), Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), Zika, post-flu or other events involving immunization with vaccines such as rabies vaccines (27,28), surgery and anesthesia (5).

evidence.snippet: Although well tolerated, eculizumab treatment did not show significant effects on motor function recovery compared to placebo in patients with GBS.

nodes.description: Antibodies against bacterial lipooligosaccharides (especially from Campylobacter jejuni) cross-react with gangliosides on peripheral nerves. Anti-GM1, anti-GD1a, and anti-GQ1b antibodies are associated with specific clinical subtypes.

nodes.description: The anti-GQ1b antibody syndrome spectrum encompasses Bickerstaff Brainstem Encephalitis (BBE), Miller Fisher Syndrome (MFS), and related disorders. Approximately one-third of clinically defined BBE cases are seronegative for anti-GQ1b antibodies, indicating alternative immune pathways beyond the canonical anti-GQ1b IgG-mediated complement-dependent pathway. Seronegative cases suggest additional mechanisms driving complement-mediated damage to ganglioside-rich neural structures.

evidence.snippet: Approximately one-third of clinically defined BBE cases are seronegative, suggesting alternative mechanisms.

evidence.reference_title: A unified spectrum model for the anti-GQ1b antibody syndromes: from pathophysiology to a new diagnostic framework.
evidence.snippet: Pathogenesis is primarily driven by anti-GQ1b IgG antibodies, generated following infection via molecular mimicry, which trigger complement-mediated damage to ganglioside-rich neural structures. The clinical presentation ranges from purely peripheral deficits (MFS) to severe central nervous system dysfunction (BBE), with frequent BBE-GBS overlap syndromes.
